name: Portuguese Gambit (Scandinavian)
summary: Against the king-pawn opening, Black gives a pawn for rapid development and wins it back with active pieces.

goal.title: Win the pawn back by developing fast
goal.text: Black is a pawn down on purpose. The plan is to bring pieces out with threats: the bishop jumps to the side of the board and hits White's queen, a knight attacks the extra pawn, and soon Black regains it with more active pieces. Do not waste time retreating; every move should develop a piece or hit something.
plans: Win back the extra pawn quickly with a knight or the queen.
Keep the bishop outside the pawn chain, where it stays active.
Bring out the rest of the pieces at once: a pawn move to free the bishop, the knight, then castle.
Do not spend moves chasing with the queen.

variations.name: 4.f3: kick the bishop, drop back to f5
variations.strategy: White kicks the bishop with a pawn move, which weakens White's own king side. The bishop drops back to a good square and Black opens the center with a side pawn, then recaptures with a developing move. Look for quick development and pressure on the central pawn while White's king is still in the middle.

why.Nxd5: It is the main-line Scandinavian, but this gambit develops the bishop first, with tempo, before taking back. After c4 your knight would be driven away and you would lose time.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: recapture on d5
variations.strategy: When White develops the knight, it can be pinned against the queen. Simply take the pawn back with the knight, then finish development: a pawn move to open the bishop, the bishop out, and castle. Black's pieces are healthy and White's central pawn becomes a target.

variations.name: 4.Be2: trade the bishop and take back the pawn
variations.strategy: White blocks the bishop's diagonal with a bishop. Accept the trade, take the pawn back with the queen, and develop with a threat on White's central pawn. The queen on the central square is safe because a knight supports it, and Black has equalized with easy development.

variations.name: 4.Nf3: trade the bishop for the knight
variations.strategy: Black trades the bishop for White's knight to wreck White's pawn structure, then takes the pawn back with the queen. White ends up with doubled pawns and an open king side, which are long-term weaknesses. Do not rush; play for the better structure.

variations.name: 3.Nc3: take the pawn back with the knight
variations.strategy: Black takes the pawn back at once, so material is level. Then develop calmly: a knight to the center, a bishop to the side with a pin, a pawn move to open the other bishop, and castle. There is no hurry; the structure is healthy and White's central pawn becomes the target.

variations.name: 3.c4: strike back with the side pawn
variations.strategy: Black hits the extra pawn from the side and recaptures with a developing move, then grabs space in the center. If White answers with the natural-looking knight move, the central pawn push attacks it and White's knight jump loses a piece. A good example of why fast development beats a pawn.

variations.name: 3.Nc3 Nxd5 4.Nxd5: recapture with the queen
variations.strategy: Black takes the pawn back and then recaptures with the queen after the knights trade, so material is level at once. The queen comes out early, so keep it safe: take space with calm pawn moves, develop the knight and bishop, and watch for any push that would chase the queen. The pawn structure is healthy and Black has no weaknesses.

variations.name: 2.e5: develop the bishop, then hit the pawn chain
variations.strategy: White gains space with an advanced pawn, so Black plays against the pawn chain instead of fighting for the center head-on. Develop the light bishop outside the chain before it gets shut in, then strike at the base of the chain with a pawn break and add pressure on the center pawn with the queenside knight and later the queen. Black is a little cramped but has a clear plan.

variations.name: 2.Nc3: gain space and kick the knight
variations.strategy: White ignores the center pawn and develops, so Black takes space with a pawn push that attacks the knight. After the knight retreats, Black builds a strong pawn center and develops pieces behind it. The plan is simple: develop the knight and the bishop, castle, and keep the center pawns safe.
